companyDescription: Trapped-ion quantum computing · $470M remaining performance obligations (+554% YoY) · first 256-qubit Tempo system sale to University of Cambridge · September Investor Day targets 'Broad Quantum Advantage'
priceNote: Live-prices.json cache (just refreshed, <1h old). Up modestly today after a brutal stretch — down ~36% over the past month on Strait of Hormuz-driven risk-off selling across quantum names plus a short-seller report questioning Pentagon-contract exposure.
summary: IonQ has fallen ~36% over the past month — a combination of broad quantum-sector risk-off (Strait of Hormuz tensions, oil spike) and a short-seller report specifically alleging Pentagon-contract funding risk and valuation disconnection from current business performance. The fundamentals tell a more constructive story: remaining performance obligations exploded to $470M (+554% YoY), and IonQ booked its first 256-qubit Tempo system sale to the University of Cambridge — a real shift from R&D-grade testing toward commercial-scale systems. Northland Securities raised its target to $70 (from $55) citing confidence in the September Investor Day, where management aims to demonstrate 'Broad Quantum Advantage.' Analyst consensus average ~$69, implying real upside from the beaten-down price — but this remains a name with genuine, disclosed headwinds (short-seller allegations, contract-funding uncertainty) that shouldn't be waved away just because the stock looks cheap relative to target.

catalysts.name: September Investor Day — 'Broad Quantum Advantage'
catalysts.description: Management's stated goal is to demonstrate leadership toward Broad Quantum Advantage at this event. Northland Securities cited this specifically when raising its target to $70. This is the nearest scheduled catalyst, though ~2 months out.

catalysts.name: First Commercial-Scale System Sale (Tempo, 256-qubit)
catalysts.description: Sold to the University of Cambridge — signals a genuine shift from R&D-grade testing toward commercial-scale systems, a real proof point beyond the backlog-growth narrative alone.

catalysts.name: Short-Seller Report / Pentagon Contract Funding Scrutiny
catalysts.description: A short-seller report specifically alleges risks around Pentagon-related contract funding and argues the valuation has disconnected from current business performance — this is an active, unresolved overhang, not settled news, and is driving real near-term price action.

risks: A short-seller report has specifically alleged Pentagon-related contract funding risk — this is an active, contested claim, not resolved fact, but it's a real driver of the recent selloff and needs to be watched, not dismissed

Down ~36% over the past month in a 'nearly seven-week losing streak' — some of this is sector-wide risk-off (Strait of Hormuz/oil spike hit all quantum names, QBTS/RGTI/QUBT included), but the magnitude and duration suggest company-specific concerns are compounding the macro effect

Quantum computing remains a pre-mainstream-revenue technology broadly — even with $470M in remaining performance obligations, converting backlog to recognized, durable revenue at scale is still an execution risk
High-multiple, high-beta name — even a modest broad risk-off shock (like today's dense macro calendar) tends to hit speculative tech disproportionately
September Investor Day is ~8 weeks out — a long wait during which sentiment (and the unresolved short-seller allegations) could continue to weigh on the stock before the next real catalyst arrives
